title: Invoker JSON contract authoring and developer-friendly error translation
creator: Liam Chen
description: Define a concise JSON schema authoring pattern and a deterministic runtime translation layer that turns low-level validation failures into actionable, localized hints for engineers integrating tool/function calling. This ticket covers: (1) a recommended authoring format that balances expressiveness (validation rules, shapes, examples) with a compact on-wire representation for model-exposed tool manifests; (2) runtime validation modes (strict, permissive, suggestive) and how they affect request acceptance and telemetry; (3) an error translation taxonomy and user-facing message templates that can be surfaced by SDKs/console; (4) compatibility considerations and upgrade path for older manifests. Goal: reduce integration time, cut false-positive invocation failures, and make repair suggestions deterministic enough for automated remediation in SDKs.
acceptance_criteria: Publish an authoring guideline document and a canonical example manifest that compiles to the run-time schema format (doc link included in attachments)
Runtime implements three validation modes: strict (reject with detailed errors), permissive (accept and emit warnings), suggestive (attempt best-effort coercion and include remediation hints)
Error translation module returns stable error codes plus human-friendly message templates and a list of suggested edits (e.g., add missing key, coerce type, shorten string)
SDKs (JS + Python) demonstrate consistent mapping of runtime errors into idiomatic exceptions with attached remediation hints and telemetry tags
Compatibility shim that maps legacy manifest fields to the new contract format with migration warnings in console
